The evidence explicitly states that standard Gaussian Splatting attenuation is not reciprocal (i.e., $σ(x, w) ≠ σ(x, −w)$) and that this lack of reciprocity prevents the application of the Objects as Volumes (OaV) framework. It further details that the proposed method restores reciprocity by assigning a learnable oriented normal vector to each Gaussian primitive, defining an oriented attenuation model that satisfies the reciprocity condition ($σ(x, w) = σ(x, -w)$). This restoration allows for the derivation of explicit geometric fields (normals and occupancy/vacancy) via the OaV framework, which in turn enables the extraction of watertight meshes and consistent normals.
